clue.text: Paper holder found in cheese - cafes devastated

indicators.note: something devastated is wrecked, so the word before it is broken up and rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone spots a sheet of paper in the cheese after a chaotic scene that wrecked some cafes.
explanation.walkthrough: The cheese comes first and the rearranged cafes follow it to give BRIEFCASE.
explanation.definitionFit: A briefcase is a flat case for carrying documents, so it holds papers.

clue.text: A second science room is erected in wood

indicators.note: in a down entry, something erected is stood upright, so the letters read from the bottom up

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the standard abbreviation for second
a lab is a laboratory, a room for science

explanation.surface: A science room built in timber, or a laboratory put up for a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: A, S and LAB are joined and the whole string is turned upside down to read BALSA.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very light timber from a tropical American tree, used for models and rafts.

clue.text: Stint worked with rain in passage

indicators.note: worked means reshaped, like clay, so the letters are moulded into another order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spell of work done out in the rain while walking down a corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods or people in transit are on their way, in the course of their journey from one place to another.

clue.text: Like clothes in which one's not oneself

definitions.text: Like clothes in which one's not oneself

blocks.clueFragment: Like clothes in which one's not oneself
blocks.note: surface reading: garments that make you feel uncomfortable or out of character
setter's reading: you are literally dressed up as somebody else, a pirate or a clown

explanation.walkthrough: 'Not oneself' usually means feeling unwell or out of sorts; here it means wearing a costume so you appear as another person.
explanation.definitionFit: Costume worn at parties to impersonate a character, so the wearer appears to be someone different.

clue.text: Broadcast story is provider of travel experiences

blocks.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
a line is a story told to persuade, as in 'spin someone a line'

explanation.surface: A tale put out on radio or TV that serves as a travel advert.
explanation.definitionFit: A company operating scheduled flights carries passengers on journeys, so it supplies trips to customers.

clue.text: To draw out concentrate

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, to pull something out, as a tooth
second meaning: a noun, a concentrated essence such as vanilla

explanation.walkthrough: 'Concentrate' reads as a verb but works here as a noun, the thick essence of something.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for pulling something out and a noun for a strong concentrated preparation.

clue.text: The method millions follow to get a computer device

indicators.note: the millions come after, so their letter is placed at the end

blocks.note: a mode is a way or method of doing something
M is the standard abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Millions of people copy a particular technique to obtain a piece of computer kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A modem is the box that links a computer to a network over a telephone or cable line.

clue.text: Sparing mostly some ancient porcelain

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: mingy is informal British for mean or stingy, sparing with money

explanation.surface: Someone is saving most of a collection of old china.
explanation.walkthrough: Mingy loses its last letter to leave MING, the Chinese dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Ming ware is fine Chinese pottery from the Ming dynasty, 1368 to 1644, so a piece is old china.

clue.text: Conclude a bargain in a stroke

blocks.note: first meaning: from the phrase '... a hard bargain', to push a deal through
second meaning: a long hit in golf or cricket

explanation.walkthrough: 'In a stroke' suggests doing a deal instantly; 'stroke' is really a shot with a club or bat.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive a deal is to force it to a conclusion, and a drive is a powerful shot in golf, tennis or cricket.

clue.text: Find one English elm diseased in hazardous area

indicators.note: a diseased thing is out of order, so the letters gathered before it are disordered

blocks.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
E is the standard abbreviation for English
taken as written

explanation.surface: Discovering a single elm with Dutch elm disease in a dangerous spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A minefield is ground sown with explosive mines, so it is a dangerous place to walk.

clue.text: Reveal the French fashion

blocks.note: le is French for the
ton means the fashionable style or set

explanation.surface: Unveiling the latest French style at a fashion show.
explanation.definitionFit: To let on is to disclose a secret, a phrasal verb for revealing what you know.

clue.text: Memory showing strain, reportedly, after scripture lesson

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so the word is taken by its sound rather than its spelling
the strain comes after the lesson, so its letters are placed second

blocks.note: RE is religious education, the school subject
tension is strain, and the spelling here matches its sound

explanation.surface: A pupil's recall shows signs of stress following a religion class.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (religious education) is a standard school subject in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Retention is the ability to keep things in the mind, so it is a synonym of recall.

clue.text: Using detailed examination, I can't allay worries

indicators.note: to worry something is to tug it about, as a dog worries a bone, so the letters are pulled out of order

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A careful investigator admits being unable to calm someone's fears.
explanation.definitionFit: An analytical approach breaks a subject down into parts and studies each one closely.

clue.text: The old labourer's endlessly cheeky in return

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter of the word is removed
something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters run right to left

blocks.note: fresh can mean impudent, cheeky, as in 'don't get fresh with me'

explanation.surface: A worker from the past is constantly answering back.
explanation.definitionFit: A serf was a medieval farm worker bound to the land of his lord, a peasant labourer of former times.

clue.text: No fixed abode?

blocks.note: surface reading: the official phrase for a homeless person
setter's reading: a dwelling that is not fixed in place because it can be towed around

explanation.walkthrough: 'No fixed abode' is the police and court phrase for someone homeless; read literally it describes a house on wheels.
explanation.definitionFit: A large caravan used as a permanent dwelling, which can be moved from site to site.

clue.text: Book the player on the bench?

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, to book a table or seat in advance
second meaning: a substitute waiting to come on in a team game

explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a noun but is the verb for securing something in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: To reserve is to secure a place ahead of time, and a reserve is a substitute held back from the starting team.

clue.text: Entrenched element in party to raise security

blocks.note: to rear is to raise, as children or animals
a guard provides protection, security

explanation.surface: A political faction tries to tighten safety measures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To raise' is a single unit: the infinitive gives the verb with the same sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The rearguard of a party is its conservative wing, resisting change, borrowed from the troops protecting an army's back.

clue.text: Renovated turbo sale (50% off) producing riot

indicators.note: half of the word is taken away, here its first two letters
renovated means rebuilt, so the letters are put together in a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written before half is removed

explanation.surface: A refurbished turbocharged car reduced by half in a sale causes a disturbance.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouble can mean public disorder or unrest, as in 'trouble on the streets', a loose synonym for a riot.

clue.text: Drinks supplier, having made profit, discussed terms

blocks.note: a bar serves drinks
to gain is to make a profit

explanation.surface: A pub, after doing well financially, negotiated a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To bargain is to haggle over the conditions of a deal, so having bargained is having negotiated.

clue.text: "In this part I steal the show" (stage performer)

indicators.note: the answer sits inside this run of words, spanning the gaps between them

blocks.note: the letters run from inside the first word to inside the last

explanation.surface: An actor boasts that this role lets them upstage everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional entertainer such as a singer or dancer who performs for an audience.

clue.text: Sheep's roaming round university in ancient city

indicators.note: roaming means wandering, so the letters stray from their order
round means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go around the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A flock wanders around a college campus in a historic town.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephesus was a great Greek city on the coast of Asia Minor, now ruins in Turkey.

clue.text: Made a vibrating noise? Sounds like conversation

indicators.note: these words say plainly that the answer is heard as another word

blocks.note: a word is a brief conversation, as in 'can I have a word?'

explanation.surface: Something buzzed, and it sounded like people talking.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech, which drops the R, the two words sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To whirr is to make a continuous low buzzing sound, like a fan or a motor spinning.

clue.text: Hostel heads fighting over muddled ends

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means placed above, so the fighting comes first
muddled means confused, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: war is fighting between nations
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: The people running hostels are squabbling about loose ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A warden is the person in charge of a youth hostel or residence hall, its manager.

clue.text: Glamour is a kind of security

blocks.note: first meaning: thin gold coating, so superficial glitter
second meaning: a ...-edged British government bond

explanation.walkthrough: Gilts are UK government bonds, called gilt-edged because they are so safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilt is surface glitter or attractiveness, and in finance it names a low-risk British government stock.

clue.text: With cargo on board, left port

blocks.note: L is the standard abbreviation for left
Aden is a port city in Yemen

explanation.surface: A loaded ship departed from the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left port' reads as a ship sailing off, but it is two pieces: an abbreviation and a named harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means loaded or carrying a heavy burden, so a laden ship has its freight aboard.

clue.text: Make worker pay - he's leader of a group

blocks.note: first meaning, read as two words: to bill a labourer, charge being make pay and hand being worker
second meaning: the foreman of a small team of workmen

explanation.walkthrough: A hand is a worker, as in farmhand, and to charge someone is to make them pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A chargehand is a workman put in charge of a small gang, ranking just below a foreman.

clue.text: Painter/drawer taking in river

indicators.note: taking in means admitting inside, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: Dr is the abbreviation for the drawer of a cheque or bill
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: An artist who sketches by the riverside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' looks like a second word for artist, but here it is the person who writes a cheque. The answer is Albrecht Dürer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dürer was the German Renaissance artist famous for his engravings and woodcuts.

clue.text: Refuse study year

blocks.note: a den is a private room for work, a study
Y is the standard abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Declining to spend a year studying.
explanation.definitionFit: To deny is to turn down a request, so it shares the verb sense of rejecting something.

clue.text: The Sir in "Dear Sir"?

blocks.note: surface reading: a knight or schoolmaster honoured with a title
setter's reading: the opening of a letter, where Sir is the person written to

explanation.walkthrough: The capital S makes 'Sir' look like a title; in a letter's greeting it simply names the recipient.
explanation.definitionFit: The person to whom a letter is sent is the one greeted as Sir at its top.

clue.text: One possessing new switch in gold

indicators.note: to switch is to swap around, so the letters change places
in means placed inside, so the shuffled letters go within the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: Someone who has a brand-new gold light switch.
explanation.definitionFit: An owner is a person who holds property, someone to whom things belong.

clue.text: Shabby boat losing last bit of polish

indicators.note: the last bit is only the final letter of the word that follows
losing means giving something up, so that letter is taken out

blocks.note: a dinghy is a small boat
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A tatty little craft that has lost the last of its varnish.
explanation.definitionFit: Dingy means drab and dirty-looking, faded, so it is a synonym of shabby.

clue.text: Attachment for hose

blocks.note: surface reading: a nozzle or fitting on a garden hose
setter's reading: hose as stockings, held up by an elastic strap

explanation.walkthrough: Hose suggests a garden pipe, but it is also the old word for stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspender is an elastic strap with a clip that holds up a stocking, fastened to a belt.
